newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sets going 14th century water clock.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sets going 14th century water clock.

text.p: Two experts from Germany and Italy have restored to working order a 14th century Moroccan water clock which has been idle for centuries, the official news agency MAP said on Thursday.
The clock had been kept in the room of the Muaqqit, the man responsible for setting hours for prayers, in Quarrawiyiin mosque in the central city of Fez.

Made in the year 1317, the clock is constructed of cedarwood with two pottery containers at different heights linked by a copper tube. Water, regulated by the tube, dripped from one container to the other and then into a third on which were marked minutes and hours, MAP said.
It named the experts as Lutz Kottoff from Germany and Italian Michel Bellomo and said they had also made a copy of the clock to be shown in the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca.
